100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On September 30, 1926, the United States government announced new immigration restrictions, tightening the quotas imposed by the Immigration Act of 1924, aiming to limit the influx of certain nationalities. In Europe, the British Empire faced rising tensions as labor strikes continued to disrupt coal production, prompting fears of a winter shortage. Meanwhile, in Germany, the political climate remained unstable, with the rise of extremist parties causing concern among moderate leaders.
